_README: The manifest that decides what news matters. YAAIN's filter reads THIS, not a hardcoded prompt. If you install something on brownie or the studio, or pin/upgrade a tool, UPDATE THIS FILE IN THE SAME BREATH — otherwise YAAIN decays into exactly the staleness it exists to prevent. Last audited against the machines: 2026-09-14 (refs/yaain-review-2026-09-14.md). Prior audit 2026-08-30 (refs/yaain-landscape-review-2026-08-30.md part (a)). AND WHEN YOU ADD A MODEL, WRITE ITS `chosen` BLOCK IN THE SAME COMMIT — the reason, the date, and a pointer to the entry that records it. A model with no recorded reason is one nobody can supersede on purpose later; if there genuinely was no decision, say so.

machines.name: studio
machines.role: local text inference for the whole fleet
machines.ceiling: ~96GB wired practical; ~100GB observed stall point. The real constraint is reading speed (~180 tok/s), not memory.

machines.name: brownie
machines.hardware: NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti, 16GB VRAM, 64GB RAM, Windows 11, Blackwell sm_120
machines.ceiling: 16GB VRAM is a HARD WALL. A model needing 24GB is unusable to us at any price. Python 3.13.14 / torch 2.13.0+cu130 — an ABI mismatch is real breakage, not a detail.

models.name: qwen3.8
models.detail: `bosun-brain` is **qwen3.8:27b-mlx** (Apple MLX build, nvfp4, 18.2GB on disk / ~19.4GB resident) at a PINNED num_ctx of 98,304 — without that pin Hermes auto-detects the training max. Also on the studio: qwen3.8:latest (Q4_K_M), and the qwen3.6 line (27b-bf16 / 27b-coding-bf16 / 27b-q8_0 / 27b-q4_K_M / 35b-a3b MoE) kept as rollback.
models.used_by: Bosun's own brain; repo-hunter enrich+explain; mac-hunter llm_generic; takomagether social drafts + council attribution

chosen.why: Em's call, taken in two steps on the same day. qwen3.8 over qwen3.6 on QUALITY: it beats 3.6 on all nine shared published benchmarks. Then MLX over GGUF on MEASURED SPEED, head to head at the same model and window — read 198.3/181.7/143.3 tok/s at 22K/45K/90K against GGUF's 179.2/164.0/139.9, and WROTE at 28.8 vs 15.7 tok/s, 83% faster. The 'MLX prefill collapses past 40K' claim that had justified a move back to GGUF is FALSE on this machine at every depth Bosun can reach. ⚠️ KNOWINGLY BOUGHT: nvfp4 has no published quality figures from anyone, for any model, where Q4_K_M does — a measured speed paid for with a quality assurance given up.
chosen.ref: observations.md 2026-09-12 (three entries); refs/studio-model-choice-2026-09-12.md; refs/exec-2026-09-13-bosun-brain-swap.md (EXECUTED — corrects its own handoff in four places); tracker bosun-brain-qwen38
chosen.revisit_if: a newer Qwen generation clears the same bars (Apache-2.0, ungated, ~27B class, served by Ollama), OR published quality figures appear for nvfp4 and contradict the bet. ⚠️ Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (180B) and Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B do NOT clear them — both are far beyond 128GB at any quantisation, and both carry an 'other' licence rather than Apache-2.0. Behaviour DID shift between formats: the MLX brain refused the watchdog's bare-token health check as injection-shaped where the GGUF brain complied. The probe was at fault and is fixed.

models.licence: Apache-2.0, ungated (the 27B line). NB the Flash-Next and 2.4T flagships are licensed "other", not Apache-2.0.

chosen.why: The Apache-2.0 default for image generation in the render-PC plan, which treated licensing as a hard spec rather than a preference. The traps it was chosen against were the popular ones — FLUX.1 [dev] and FLUX.2 klein are non-commercial.
chosen.revisit_if: a successor at a licence at least as clean that still fits 16GB

models.name: Wan 2.2
models.detail: 14B suite (t2v/i2v/fun-control/fun-camera x high+low) + 5B ti2v/fun_control + Wan 2.1 VACE 1.3B. PLUS Wan2.2-Animate-14B Q4_K_M (11.5GB GGUF, QuantStack, apache-2.0, ungated) added 2026-08-31 for pose-driven character animation, with clip_vision_h and the DWPose extractor (comfyui_controlnet_aux). Animate loads via UnetLoaderGGUF, the route proven by LTX-2.3 the same day.

chosen.why: The Apache-2.0 default for video in the render-PC plan; installed and proven on brownie 2026-08-14 onward.
chosen.revisit_if: a Wan successor, or another video model, at a licence at least as clean. NOTE Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B is a PLACEHOLDER repo (0 downloads, no parameter count) despite ComfyUI shipping a WanAnimate2ToVideo node — do not plan around it. Wan2.2-S2V-14B (speech-to-video) is clean and NOT installed: Em's open call, adjacency to council clips and narrated promos.

models.name: LTX-2.3
models.detail: LTX-2.3 22B dev + distilled Q4_K_M + a 7.6GB distilled LoRA. LOADS VIA UnetLoaderGGUF, not UNETLoader. RUN + MEASURED 2026-08-31: ~30s warm for a 4.84s clip at 768x512/25fps, peak VRAM 15,215 MiB of 16,303 — ~3x faster than Wan ti2v_5B. Text encoder is DualCLIPLoaderGGUF type=ltxv (gemma GGUF + embeddings connector); the LTX-native loaders are closed to us because they want a full safetensors checkpoint in checkpoints/. VIDEO ONLY — the audio path needs one of those closed loaders. Graph: hermes/workflows/ltx2.3-t2v-gguf.api.json

chosen.why: Installed as a second video path alongside Wan 2.2, notably for joint audio+video. RUN 2026-08-31 and it is the faster path for short clips (~3x Wan at comparable resolution), so it earns its place.
chosen.revisit_if: LTX-2.5 (created 2026-07-23, gated=auto, same Community licence family) is the successor and ComfyUI shipped day-0 support. The IC-LoRAs (Clean-Plate, Relight) are likely better value than the version bump — they add capability to the 2.3 we already have. Both need Em's HF click-through. Also open: wiring LTX's audio path, which needs the safetensors checkpoint.

models.licence: LTX-2 Community License Agreement — worldwide, royalty-free, NO territorial exclusion; paid licence required only above $10M annual revenue. Read 2026-08-31. Clean for us.

models.name: Hunyuan3D 2.0
models.detail: DiT v2.0, shape + texture. LICENCE UNRESOLVED: Tencent Community licence excludes the EU/UK/South Korea including the OUTPUT — awaiting Em's ruling.

chosen.why: Installed and proven end to end (shape AND texture) the same night. LICENCE UNRESOLVED AND IT IS EM'S CALL: the Tencent Community licence permits commercial use under 1M MAU but territorially excludes the EU, UK and South Korea, and extends that to the OUTPUT — i.e. you may not display results there. That is the same shape as the MiniMax H3 licence a model was deleted over the same day, and a public website is displayed in the UK/EU by definition.
chosen.revisit_if: Em rules on the territorial licence, OR a licence-clean successor appears. NOTE: tencent/Hy4-preview is NOT that successor — it is a 780B text model. Tencent's real 3D line is Hunyuan3D-2.1, published 2025-06-13, i.e. older than this choice.

models.name: TRELLIS.2 (trellis.cpp)
models.detail: trellis.cpp v0.6.0 (installed 2026-08-29), MIT, standalone C++/GGML, no Python/torch — so it cannot disturb ComfyUI. We run the f16 weights (~16.5GB); q8 (~9.5GB) and q4 (~6GB) exist since v0.5.4 via the installer's --quant flag and would sit well under the 16GB VRAM wall. The Python wrapper route is DEAD on our torch 2.13 ABI.

chosen.why: Chosen as the LICENCE-CLEAN image-to-3D path, deliberately alongside Hunyuan3D rather than instead of it: MIT end to end (trellis.cpp, TRELLIS.2-4B, BiRefNet), and it uses ungated mirrors so it needs no DINOv3 licence click. A standalone C++/GGML binary with no Python or torch, so it cannot disturb the ComfyUI install — which is also why it sidesteps the torch-ABI wall that killed the Python wrapper route.
chosen.revisit_if: quality proves inadequate against Hunyuan3D, or the Hunyuan3D licence is ruled clean. Quality caveat softened 2026-08-30: the maintainer measured statistical parity with the reference pipeline at v0.4.3 (multi-seed, matched-conditioning A/B), but CUDA geometry then regressed at v0.5.4 and was fixed at v0.6.0 with no restated parity measurement, so parity is claimed for a build one regression-and-fix behind ours. Our own evidence on v0.6.0 is Em's by-sight approval of the pipe-holder render (2026-08-30), not a measurement.

models.name: Qwen2.5-VL-7B
models.detail: Apache-2.0, 16.6GB, one-shot by design (a resident critic would pin ~16GB on our only render tier)
models.used_by: the video judge; NDN's design critic

chosen.why: Chosen for the vision tier because licence is a hard spec: Apache-2.0 and ungated, verified against BOTH the model card and the HF API rather than one page-read. Picked over Gemma 3, which is gated and use-restricted — the same class of problem that got MiniMax H3 deleted the day before. It also installs nothing, running on the Python/torch/transformers already on brownie.
chosen.revisit_if: a replacement is proposed — re-run the discriminating two-image test in brownie/README.md first. 'It described something reasonable' is not a pass; the failure mode being guarded against is a model that answers fluently about a picture it never saw.

models.name: gemma-3-12b
models.detail: gemma-3-12b-it + mmproj — LTX-2.3's text encoder, PROVEN IN USE 2026-08-31 via DualCLIPLoaderGGUF type=ltxv

chosen.why: NOT A CHOICE — it arrived as LTX-2.3's required text encoder. Its TEXT role is proven working (2026-08-31, the LTX run). Its VISION weights remain unusable to us (the GGUF mmproj is transposed by ComfyUI-GGUF, and the Gemma3 commits in that repo add text support only), which is why the vision tier is a separate Qwen2.5-VL model.
chosen.revisit_if: LTX is replaced or upgraded — this follows whatever LTX needs

tools.name: Ollama
tools.detail: serves every studio model, tailnet-bound. num_ctx pins and keep-alive behaviour are load-bearing for us. Running the MLX engine on Apple silicon since 2026-09-12 — so Ollama's MLX work is no longer a preview we are watching, it is the engine under Bosun's brain.

tools.name: ComfyUI
tools.detail: brownie's generation front end, portable install, tailnet-only, NO AUTH (the bind is the security)

tools.name: ComfyUI-GGUF
tools.detail: provides UnetLoaderGGUF + DualCLIPLoaderGGUF — THE ONLY WAY our LTX-2.3 model AND its gemma text encoder load. Re-verified 2026-09-14 against the GitHub API: upstream HEAD is STILL 6ea2651 of 2026-01-12, and we sit exactly on it. Unmaintained (8 months) but NOT stale — there is nothing to take. ⚠️ The Gemma3 12B commits are ALREADY INSTALLED and add TEXT support only; they do NOT fix the transposed vision mmproj. If a 'new ComfyUI-GGUF commit' ever appears in the feed again, check the commit DATE before believing maintenance resumed — the 2026-08-30 first poll reported these January commits as news.

tools.detail: the GGUF lineage everything we quantise depends on

tools.name: transformers
tools.detail: 5.14.1 on brownie — the vision tier runs on it. Do NOT pip install into brownie's interpreter without --target.

tools.name: torch
tools.detail: 2.13.0+cu130 on brownie. A wheel built for another torch is a hard failure (this killed the TRELLIS.2 wrapper route).

tools.name: Claude Code

The Mini runs 2.1.197 (2026-09-14), which is ~70 releases behind.

tools.name: Hermes Agent
tools.detail: PINNED v0.20.6 — verified live on the harness 2026-09-14 (/health reports 0.20.6). NEVER AUTO-UPDATE: our loop patches are re-applied by hand after any update. ⚠️ DO NOT TAKE 0.21.x YET — v0.21.0 was a ~5,800-commit rewrite and v0.21.2 is the patch fixing state.db fragility that v0.21.0 itself introduced. Revisit when 0.21.x has been quiet for a few weeks. (This line said 'PINNED v0.20.1 at commit f80f453a' until 2026-09-14, two weeks after the pin actually moved — which is why every 0.20.x patch release read as news.)

tools.name: comfyui_controlnet_aux + segment-anything-2 + VideoHelperSuite
tools.detail: Added to brownie 2026-08-31 for the Wan Animate pipeline. DWPreprocessor extracts the pose skeleton that DRIVES Animate; SAM2 masks the character; VHS is video I/O. Installed behind a pip constraints file pinning torch/torchvision/numpy/transformers because controlnet_aux's requirements list unpinned torch -- the freeze diff was additions only, 0 changes, and LTX-2.3 re-ran clean as a regression check. FaceMaskFromPoseKeypoints was deliberately NOT installed (it needs ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper, a 34MB parallel Wan implementation, for one OPTIONAL input).

constraints: VRAM <= 16GB on brownie. This is the single most important filter on relevance — most model announcements are written for 24-80GB cards. A quantisation that brings a model under 16GB is itself the news.

LICENCE IS A HARD SPEC, NOT A PREFERENCE. Apache-2.0 and MIT are the defaults. TERRITORIAL RESTRICTIONS ARE DISQUALIFYING - MiniMax H3 was deleted over exactly this (2026-08-29), and Hunyuan3D 2.0's territorial exclusion of the EU/UK/South Korea is still awaiting a ruling. A gated model costs a human licence click.
Blackwell sm_120 compatibility on brownie is real breakage, not a footnote.
brownie runs Python 3.13.14 / torch 2.13.0+cu130. Wheels built for another torch do not load.
Off-API preference: local first, metered only where metering is the point.
Loader dependencies matter as much as models (LTX-2.3 loads through UnetLoaderGGUF, not UNETLoader).

licence_policy.disqualifying: any territorial restriction on use OR on the output; any non-commercial clause
licence_policy.needs_human: gated models (a licence click), and any bespoke community licence

_CHOSEN: Every model carries a dated `chosen` block: WHY we picked it, WHEN, a pointer to the dated entry that is the real record, and where known what would supersede it. The point is that when something newer appears we can weigh it against the reason rather than just mute it. Where no decision was ever recorded the block SAYS SO rather than inventing one. The `ref` is a pointer, never a restatement — the journal entry is the source of record.

retired.name: MiniMax H3
retired.why: DELETED, Em's call, on licence: the MiniMax H3 Community Licence carries territorial and commercial-use restrictions, which makes it unusable for a publication. 39.56GB reclaimed across four files; it had never been run, and LTX-2 also does joint audio+video, which was its distinguishing feature. Recorded because it is the strongest precedent we have for licence-as-a-hard-spec — and so a successor is not proposed without reading its licence first.
